newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria appoints four insurers for state oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria appoints four insurers for state oil firm.

text.p: Nigeria's oil ministry on Monday appointed a consortium of four insurance firms to insure the assets of state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
This puts paid to a longstanding controversy over who should handle the oil company's lucrative insurance account.

The appointment was made known in a statement by the oil ministry, barely a week after an earlier directive from finance minister Anthony Ani that all federal government property must be insured by the government-owned National Insurance Corporation of Nigeria (NICON).
The consortium of local insurers comprises Industrial and General Insurance Limited, UNIC Insurance Plc, Kapital Insurance Company Limited and Inter-Continental Assurance Company Limited.
The statement said the decision was informed by "the need to develop the local insurance market, spread the risk and also put in place an efficient insurance service.

"As far as the Ministry of Petroleum Resources and the federal government are concerned, the issue of who is to insure NNPC's assets has been resolved once and for all," it said, adding "The insurance matter remains closed and put behind us."

But the matter remains pending before the Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal, following NICON's appeal against an earlier ruling denying it the right to insure NNPC's assets in favour of the four companies named in the consortium.
The NNPC insurance account is worth 2.025 billion naira.
NNPC, 100 percent owned by the federal government, pumps two million barrels of crude oil daily, which accounts for more than 90 percent of Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings.
Its assets include oil refineries, petrochemical plants, oil depots and sundry other properties.
NICON, Nigeria's biggest insurance firm is 100 percent federal government-owned.
